Islands & water

Batu Kareta Island

Batu Kareta, also written Batu Kereta, is part of the Carocok bay area. Government reporting in 2020 describes bridges and small jetties linking the beach and Batu Kereta, followed by a boat crossing to Cingkuak.

Updated · 27 November 2026

Two islands, different access

Batu Kareta and Cingkuak are different places. The 2020 report links Batu Kereta with the beach’s bridge network, while Cingkuak is reached by boat. Separate your walking plan from a boat crossing.

Check the path on arrival

Facilities described in an older report may have sections closed today. Watch for barriers, slippery surfaces and pedestrian traffic; avoid stopping for photographs where passengers board.

Alternative

Bay landscape

As part of the bay landscape, the point can enrich observation from Pantai Carocok without a separate crossing.

Questions

Before you go

01Can Batu Kareta be visited?+

Government reporting describes access through the beach bridge network. Follow signs and staff directions for sections open on your visit.

02Is there a bridge there?+

Yes. The government report of 16 August 2020 describes bridges and small jetties linking the beach area, including Batu Kereta. Check current access on arrival.

03How is it different from Cingkuak?+

Government reporting describes Batu Kareta within the bridge network, while Cingkuak is a boat destination. Check pedestrian access and boat services separately.

04Where to view it?+

From the edge of Pantai Carocok, the bay faces several island points. Use it for landscape observation.
